Writing about keys is not the same as committing one. Every line below failed
the repository before the rule required a PEM header.

  Store the PRIVATE KEY in a hardware security module, never in the repo.
  The CERTIFICATE chain must be complete before deployment.
  Pass BEGIN RSA to openssl to start the block.

A public certificate is published by design and is not a secret, so it is
worth noting rather than blocking:

-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
MIIBkTCB+wIJAKZfixtureonlynotarealcertificatefixtureonlynotareal
-----END CERTIFICATE-----

A PEM header can also appear as a file-type SIGNATURE, which describes how to
recognise a key file rather than containing one. This is the shared-mime-info
database, found by scanning 3362 real XML files - two of them failed on it:

  <mime type="application/pgp-keys" magic="-----BEGIN PGP PRIVATE KEY BLOCK-----" />
  <match type="string" value="-----BEGIN PGP PRIVATE KEY BLOCK-----" offset="0"/>

Documentation shows the key format with a placeholder body. This is npm's own
configuration reference, which three of 388 real HTML files on this host
reproduce - a PEM header followed by XXXX, not a key:

  key="-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----\nXXXX\nXXXX\n-----END PRIVATE KEY-----"
